body:
## Signal (from the wyrd instance)

The instance's only CI-parity gate delegates wholesale to the host's single-sourced runner (`C4-ci` → `cargo xtask ci`). But the host repo also runs **always-on CI jobs outside that runner** (a `typos` spell-check job, a `docs-check` lint/render job). Nothing in the harness models "host CI jobs the delegated runner does not cover", so bundles passed Check green and `pdca publish` opened PRs that immediately failed a required status. It happened four times, always the same gate (`typos`): getwyrd/wyrd#595, #564, #569, and historically #394.

## Why the existing hooks don't catch it

- The **T4 contribution gate** (`publish._t4_passes`) is the natural pre-push slot, but it runs with `cwd=cfg.root` **before** `patch.diff` is applied to the clean base branch — the failing prose arrives *in the patch*, so a T4 command cannot see it. (It also has zero configured gates by default, so it is vacuous unless an instance adds rows.)
- The **C4 re-gate** covers exactly what the host runner covers; anything the host keeps in separate CI jobs is structurally out of reach, and nothing surfaces that residue to the instance author.

## Instance-level workaround applied in wyrd

The host repo extended its own runner to include the missing jobs (getwyrd/wyrd#598 / PR #599: `typos` + docs lint/render inside `cargo xtask ci`, required-in-CI / warn-skip-locally), and the instance's INTEGRATION map now documents the composition. That fixes wyrd — but only because the host repo was willing to change; the harness still cannot express the gap.

## Proposal (either/both)

1. **Declared host-only CI commands:** an instance-config list (e.g. `[gates.host_ci]`) of commands the harness runs as a **pre-publish gate against the tree with `patch.diff` applied** (an isolated worktree, the same machinery the verify leg uses) — closing the T4 slot's pre-apply blindness.
2. **Composition audit:** `pdca gates` (or `pdca doctor`) cross-checks the host's CI workflow files against the delegated runner's coverage and warns about always-on jobs that appear in neither the runner nor the declared host-only list — so the residue is at least visible instead of silent.

Motivation for doing it in the harness: every rendered instance whose host keeps *any* gate outside the single-sourced runner has this exact blind spot today.
title: Host CI jobs outside the delegated gate runner are invisible to the pipeline — published PRs can open red
